var(--border)}\n.inline-code:hover{color:var(--accent);border-bottom-color:var(--accent)}\n\n@media(max-width:600px){\n  h1{font-size:1.5rem}\n  h2{font-size:1.25rem}\n  .results-table{font-size:14px}\n}\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n\n<a href=\"#main\" class=\"skip-link\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<nav class=\"side-nav\" data-scrollspy aria-label=\"Section navigation\">\n  <a href=\"#hero\">Overview</a>\n  <a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a>\n  <a href=\"#method\">Method</a>\n  <a href=\"#results\">Results</a>\n  <a href=\"#figures\">Figures</a>\n  <a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a>\n</nav>\n\n<main id=\"main\">\n\n<!-- ═══════════════════ HERO ═══════════════════ -->\n<section id=\"hero\" class=\"hero\">\n  <h1>Host vocabulary predicts whether new scientific concepts take root across disciplinary boundaries</h1>\n\n  <p class=\"tldr\">When a scientific concept first appears in a new field, do the words around it at the moment of arrival predict whether anyone in that field will pick it up? This study tracked 426 emerging concepts and 462,812 works across physics, computer science, and biomedicine. The share of a concept's initial partner terms belonging to the host field's own vocabulary predicts five-year newcomer uptake. On an independent biomedical replication of 191 MeSH concepts, each standard deviation of host-vocabulary share raises newcomer uptake by 23% (incidence-rate ratio 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36).</p>\n\n  <div class=\"hero-links\">\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n    <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L\">Code repository</a>\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/exec_summary.pdf\">Read the executive summary</a>\n  </div>\n  <p class=\"round-links\">Round reports:\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-1/report.pdf\">Round 1</a> &middot;\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-2/report.pdf\">Round 2</a> &middot;\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-3/report.pdf\">Round 3</a> &middot;\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-4/report.pdf\">Round 4</a> &middot;\n    <a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new@fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-5/report.pdf\">Round 5</a>\n  </p>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ═══════════════════ CONTRIBUTIONS ═══════════════════ -->\n<section id=\"contributions\">\n  <h2>Contributions</h2>\n  <div class=\"cards\">\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Host-entry grafting predicts uptake</h3>\n      <p>A <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-3/experiment-7\">pre-registered host-entry test</a> showing that the host-vocabulary composition of a concept's initial partners predicts newcomer uptake, <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-4/experiment-9\">replicated</a> on an independent MeSH biomedical population (co-primary IRR 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36; verdict: REPLICATED). Development-set estimates concordant: Screen IRR 1.30, <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-4/evaluation-2\">Held-out</a> IRR 1.19.</p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Outcome-blind concept dataset</h3>\n      <p>A semantically grounded, outcome-blind <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-2/dataset-5\">dataset of 426 emerging concepts</a> with 462,812 OpenAlex works and an independent <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-1/dataset-3\">191-concept MeSH biomedical check population</a>.</p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Host-specific, dual-margin effect</h3>\n      <p>The host-vocabulary effect is host-specific (though the Balassa-index lift leg is near-collinear with the continuous share) and operates through both the <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-5/evaluation-6\">extensive and intensive margins</a>, with <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-5/evaluation-7\">no detectable variation</a> by origin field.</p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Persistent-neighbour closure predicts emergence</h3>\n      <p>General closure fails on the Held-out fold while the panel coefficient for <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-3/experiment-5\">persistent-neighbour closure is significant</a> (&minus;1.07, Holm <em>p</em> = 0.015; development-set estimate), and the effect is <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-4/evaluation-3\">not Burt brokerage</a>.</p>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"card\">\n      <h3>Diffusion typology and adopter enrichment</h3>\n      <p>A stable <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-3/experiment-8\">two-type diffusion typology</a> (localised vs. broad), an expansion-before-diffusion ordering, <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-4/evaluation-4\">adopter-level enrichment</a> for prior partner exposure (OR 3.09; prevalence 0.79 vs. 0.61), and <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-4/evaluation-5\">four representative cases</a>.</p>\n    </div>\n\n  </div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ═══════════════════ METHOD ═══════════════════ -->\n<section id=\"method\">\n  <h2>Method</h2>\n\n  <figure class=\"fig-inline\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 1: Study design and analysis pipeline\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Diagram of the four-stage study pipeline: data assembly from OpenAlex, co-word network construction with Leiden communities, matched event study for emergence precursors, and PPML regression for host-entry grafting\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 1.</strong> Overview of the study design. (a) Data: an outcome-blind arXiv concept pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts, split into a screen fold (247) and a held-out fold (119), and an independent MeSH biomedical check population of 191 concepts. Both are drawn from 462,812 OpenAlex works. (b) Co-word network: yearly co-word snapshots (25 snapshots, ~27k nodes, ~84k edges) with Leiden communities. (c) RQ1, emergence precursors: a matched event study compares closure measures in the pre-onset window between concepts showing sustained uptake and controls. (d) RQ2, host-entry grafting: a concept enters a non-origin host subfield; the host-vocabulary share is the exposure in a pre-registered PPML regression predicting 5-year newcomer uptake.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <p>The study proceeds in four stages (Figure 1). An outcome-blind pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts was <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-1/dataset-1\" class=\"inline-code\">assembled</a> from OpenAlex titles and abstracts (first appearance 2005&ndash;2016, 20&ndash;300 papers in the first-appearance window), split into a Screen fold (247) and a Held-out fold (119). An independent biomedical arm of <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-1/dataset-3\" class=\"inline-code\">191 MeSH concepts</a> was drawn from new MeSH descriptors. The combined corpus comprises <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-2/dataset-5\" class=\"inline-code\">462,812 unique OpenAlex works</a>. A <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-2/experiment-1\" class=\"inline-code\">logistic-regression classifier</a> (F1 = 0.82, AUC = 0.89) and a variant merger (B-cubed F1 = 0.78) grounded every concept. The pool is dominated by physics and computer-science concepts from arXiv.</p>\n\n  <p>From 259,716 design-weighted background works, 25 yearly three-year-window <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-2/experiment-3\" class=\"inline-code\">co-occurrence snapshots</a> were built (approximately 27,000 nodes and 84,000 edges per snapshot), with association-strength edge weights and Leiden community detection.</p>\n\n  <p><strong>RQ1: Emergence precursors.</strong> For each concept showing sustained uptake (at least 20 papers per year plus at least 20 percentile points in co-word network strength), a matched control was drawn from the same first-appearance band and origin field. The standardised mean difference in closure measures between treated and control concepts at lags &minus;3 to 0 is the event-study estimand. Four closure variants were computed: general, turnover-residualised, persistent-neighbour (restricted to top-20 neighbours present in consecutive years), and Burt constraint.</p>\n\n  <p><strong>RQ2: Host-entry grafting.</strong> A host-entry event is the first year a concept appears in a non-origin subfield with at least five co-occurring partner terms. Host-vocabulary share is the tag-weighted mean of each partner's pre-entry publication share in the host subfield. The outcome is five-year newcomer uptake: the count of papers by author-disjoint newcomers. A Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood (PPML) regression with concept-clustered standard errors tests whether host-vocabulary share predicts uptake. Two specifications were pre-registered: a primary (concept-by-year and host-by-year fixed effects) and a co-primary (concept, entry-year, and host fixed effects), the latter declared for use when the primary drops below 30 concept clusters.</p>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ═══════════════════ RESULTS ═══════════════════ -->\n<section id=\"results\">\n  <h2>Results</h2>\n\n  <h3>Structural precursors of emergence</h3>\n\n  <p>On the Held-out fold (a development-set estimate; the fold was used in pipeline development), only persistent-neighbour closure survives Holm correction: the panel coefficient is &minus;1.07 (Holm <em>p</em> = 0.015) and the matched event-study standardised mean difference is &minus;0.83 (95% CI [&minus;1.71, &minus;0.10]). General closure is not significant (Holm <em>p</em> = 0.147), and neither is turnover-residualised closure (Holm <em>p</em> = 0.635). Burt constraint has a positive sign (+0.11, 95% CI [0.02, 0.19]), indicating that emerging concepts sit in more constrained, not more brokered, ego networks. The picture is of open, fast-renewing connections among a concept's most strongly associated terms within a dense wider ego network.</p>\n\n  <p>The <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-2/experiment-4\" class=\"inline-code\">MeSH closure replication</a> is directional under a sensitivity label (<em>D</em> = &minus;0.42, Holm <em>p</em> = 0.039, <em>n</em> = 29) but null under the primary label (<em>D</em> = &minus;0.09, Holm <em>p</em> = 0.677, <em>n</em> = 15). Structural precursors add no predictive value beyond frequency, burst, degree and entropy baselines (logistic AUC 0.89 vs. 0.88).</p>\n\n  <h3>Host-entry grafting</h3>\n\n  <div class=\"table-wrap\">\n  <table class=\"results-table\" aria-label=\"Host-entry grafting results across folds and specifications\">\n    <thead>\n      <tr><th>Fold</th><th>Specification</th><th>IRR/SD</th><th>95% CI</th><th><em>p</em></th></tr>\n    </thead>\n    <tbody>\n      <tr><td>Screen</td><td>Co-primary</td><td class=\"num\">1.30</td><td class=\"num\">1.16&ndash;1.45</td><td class=\"num\">&lt;0.001</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Held-out</td><td>Co-primary</td><td class=\"num\">1.19</td><td class=\"num\">1.06&ndash;1.33</td><td class=\"num\">0.004</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Held-out</td><td>Primary (strict FE)</td><td class=\"num\">0.98</td><td class=\"num\">0.70&ndash;1.37</td><td class=\"num\">0.91</td></tr>\n      <tr class=\"hl\"><td>MeSH</td><td>Co-primary</td><td class=\"num\">1.23</td><td class=\"num\">1.12&ndash;1.36</td><td class=\"num\">&lt;0.001</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>MeSH</td><td>Primary</td><td class=\"num\">1.32</td><td class=\"num\">1.10&ndash;1.60</td><td class=\"num\">0.004</td></tr>\n      <tr class=\"hl\"><td>Pooled (IVW)</td><td>Co-primary</td><td class=\"num\">1.26</td><td class=\"num\">1.17&ndash;1.36</td><td class=\"num\">&lt;0.001</td></tr>\n    </tbody>\n  </table>\n  </div>\n\n  <figure class=\"fig-inline\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 4: Host-vocabulary effect across folds\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig4_v0.png\" alt=\"Forest plot of host-vocabulary incidence-rate ratios across Screen, Held-out, and MeSH folds with confidence intervals, showing the pooled estimate at 1.26\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 4.</strong> Host-vocabulary effect on five-year newcomer uptake across folds and specifications. Each row gives the PPML incidence-rate ratio (IRR) per one standard deviation of host-vocabulary share, on a log axis; horizontal bars are 95% concept-clustered confidence intervals. Blue marks the OpenAlex screen and held-out folds, green the independent MeSH replication, and the amber diamond the inverse-variance weighted pooled co-primary estimate. Co-transfer (grey diamonds) is null on every fold.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <p>On the independent MeSH biomedical population, a one-standard-deviation increase in host-vocabulary share raises newcomer uptake by 23% (co-primary IRR 1.23, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.36, <em>p</em> &lt; 0.001; primary IRR 1.32, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.60; verdict: REPLICATED). Development-set estimates on the main-arm folds are concordant: Screen co-primary IRR 1.30 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.45), Held-out co-primary IRR 1.19 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.33, wild-cluster bootstrap <em>p</em> = 0.012, nativeness-permutation <em>p</em> = 0.026). The inverse-variance weighted pooled estimate is 1.26 (95% CI 1.17 to 1.36, <em>I</em><sup>2</sup> = 0). Co-transfer of origin companions is null across all folds and specifications.</p>\n\n  <p>The fully saturated primary specification on the Held-out fold is inconclusive (IRR 0.98, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.37) because it retains only 250 of 972 events with 30 concept clusters; this was declared underpowered in advance (minimum detectable effect IRR 1.30).</p>\n\n  <h3>Mechanism decomposition</h3>\n\n  <p>The host-vocabulary effect operates through both margins: the extensive-margin effect is +6.4 percentage points per SD (95% CI 4.8 to 8.1, approximately a 13% increase relative to the base rate of 51%), the intensive-margin IRR is 1.18 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.27), and the extensive margin accounts for 38% of the total effect (95% CI 21% to 55%). Adding generality controls (subfield entropy and log frequency of entry partners) retains 97% of the host-vocabulary coefficient (inverse-variance weighted retention 0.97, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.10). The Wald test for origin-field dependence is null (<em>p</em> = 0.64).</p>\n\n  <p>At the adopter level, authors who take up a concept in a new field are enriched for prior exposure to its entry partners (conditional logistic regression OR 3.09; prevalence 0.79 vs. 0.61; 95% CI 2.32 to 4.28; 1,013 matched strata, 422 entries, 109 concepts; Screen fold, not independently confirmed). The <a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_F1tk5OGtH84L/round-3/experiment-6\" class=\"inline-code\">breadth-prediction screen</a> (does pre-emergence openness predict how many new subfields a concept will reach?) found no effect beyond growth and level baselines.</p>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ═══════════════════ FIGURES ═══════════════════ -->\n<section id=\"figures\">\n  <h2>Figures</h2>\n\n  <figure class=\"gallery-fig\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 1: Study design and analysis pipeline\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Diagram of the four-stage study pipeline: data assembly from OpenAlex, co-word network construction with Leiden communities, matched event study for emergence precursors, and PPML regression for host-entry grafting\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 1.</strong> Overview of the study design. (a) Data: an outcome-blind arXiv concept pool of 426 emerging scientific concepts, split into a screen fold (247) and a held-out fold (119), and an independent MeSH biomedical check population of 191 concepts. Both are drawn from 462,812 OpenAlex works. (b) Co-word network: yearly co-word snapshots (25 snapshots, ~27k nodes, ~84k edges) with Leiden communities; the schematic shows three colour-coded communities. (c) RQ1, emergence precursors: a matched event study compares closure measures in the pre-onset window between concepts showing sustained uptake (blue, rising after onset) and controls (grey, flat). (d) RQ2, host-entry grafting: a concept enters a non-origin host subfield. Its partner terms are either host-native (dark green) or from the origin vocabulary (light blue). The host-vocabulary share (orange) is the exposure in a pre-registered PPML regression with concept-clustered standard errors predicting 5-year newcomer uptake. The timelines and bars in (c) and (d) are schematic and carry no data values.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <figure class=\"gallery-fig\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 2: Co-word network snapshot\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig2_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Co-word network with six colour-coded Leiden communities showing pool concepts as peripheral bridge nodes between dense clusters, with wireless backhaul, EPR steering, and holographic QCD labelled\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 2.</strong> Schematic co-word network snapshot (2012, three-year window). Nodes are concept-keyword terms and grey edges are association-strength weighted co-occurrences; node fill colour (blue, green, orange, purple, red, teal) marks Leiden community membership, and larger circles are high-degree hub terms. Background terms (plain nodes) form dense communities joined by a few inter-community edges. Pool concepts (bold black rings) sit on the periphery of communities, mostly in the gaps between two of them, where they act as bridge or connector nodes; three are labelled as examples (<em>wireless backhaul</em>, <em>EPR steering</em>, <em>holographic QCD</em>). The full network comprises approximately 27,000 nodes and 84,000 edges; the panel is a stylised rendering of its high-degree core for readability.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <figure class=\"gallery-fig\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 3: Pre-emergence closure by measure type\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig3_v0.png\" alt=\"Forest plot of pre-emergence closure measures on the held-out fold, with persistent-neighbour closure as the only measure surviving Holm correction\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 3.</strong> Pre-emergence closure on the held-out fold, by measure type. Each row shows the standardised mean difference between concepts that later show sustained uptake and matched controls. Points are estimates and horizontal bars are 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. The dashed vertical line marks no effect, and Holm-corrected <em>p</em>-values are listed to the right of the first three rows. Only persistent-neighbour closure (blue) survives Holm correction (event-study &minus;0.83, 95% CI [&minus;1.71, &minus;0.10]; panel coefficient &minus;1.07, Holm <em>p</em> = 0.015). General closure (Holm <em>p</em> = 0.147) and turnover-residualised closure (Holm <em>p</em> = 0.635) are shown in grey: they do not survive confirmation, and their intervals cross zero. Burt constraint (orange) is positive (+0.11, 95% CI [0.02, 0.19]), indicating that emerging concepts sit in more constrained, not more brokered, ego networks.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <figure class=\"gallery-fig\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 4: Host-vocabulary effect across folds\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig4_v0.png\" alt=\"Forest plot of host-vocabulary incidence-rate ratios across Screen, Held-out, and MeSH folds with confidence intervals, showing the pooled estimate at 1.26\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 4.</strong> Host-vocabulary effect on five-year newcomer uptake across folds and specifications. Each row gives the PPML incidence-rate ratio (IRR) per one standard deviation of host-vocabulary share, on a log axis; horizontal bars are 95% concept-clustered confidence intervals, and the dashed vertical line marks IRR = 1 (no effect). Filled circles are the co-primary specification (concept, entry-year and host fixed effects) and open circles the primary specification with concept-by-year and host-by-year fixed effects. Blue marks the OpenAlex screen and sealed held-out folds, green the independent MeSH replication, and the amber diamond the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) pooled co-primary estimate. The co-primary effect is significant on all three folds (screen IRR 1.30 [1.16, 1.45], held-out 1.19 [1.06, 1.33], MeSH 1.23 [1.12, 1.36]), and the pooled estimate is 1.26 [1.17, 1.36]. The primary specification is inconclusive on the held-out fold (IRR 0.98 [0.70, 1.37], 30 clusters, <em>p</em> = 0.91) but significant on MeSH (IRR 1.32 [1.10, 1.60]). Grey diamonds are the co-transfer regressor from the co-primary models. Its intervals include 1 on every fold (<em>p</em> = 0.48, 0.60 and 0.053). The right-hand columns list each estimate with its 95% CI and <em>p</em>-value.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <figure class=\"gallery-fig\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 5: Extensive and intensive margin decomposition\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig5_v0.png\" alt=\"Decomposition of the host-vocabulary effect into extensive margin at 6.43 percentage points per SD, intensive margin IRR at 1.183, and extensive share at 38 percent of total\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 5.</strong> Decomposition of the host-vocabulary effect into extensive and intensive margins across the screen, held-out and MeSH folds. Blue circles show per-fold estimates, vermillion diamonds the inverse-variance-weighted (IVW) pooled estimate, and horizontal bars 95% confidence intervals. (a) Extensive margin: linear-probability-model effect of a one-standard-deviation increase in host-vocabulary share on the probability of any newcomer uptake, in percentage points per SD (dashed line: no effect). The pooled effect is 6.43 pp (95% CI 4.76 to 8.11). (b) Intensive margin: PPML incidence-rate ratio per SD conditional on uptake, on a log axis (dashed line: IRR = 1). The pooled IRR is 1.183 (95% CI 1.104 to 1.267). All three folds are positive on both margins, and every fold interval excludes the null. (c) Share of the total effect: the extensive margin accounts for 38% (95% CI 21% to 55%, black whisker) and the intensive margin for the remaining 62%.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n  <figure class=\"gallery-fig\">\n    <button class=\"fig-trigger\" aria-label=\"Enlarge Figure 6: Four representative cases of the host-vocabulary gradient\">\n      <img src=\"figures/fig6_v0.png\" alt=\"Four representative cases showing host-vocabulary share by host entry for wireless backhaul, EPR steering, locally repairable code, and holographic QCD, with rooted entries in green and non-rooted in grey\">\n    </button>\n    <figcaption><strong>Figure 6.</strong> Four representative cases of the host-vocabulary gradient. Each panel shows one concept, and each horizontal bar is one of its host entries in the co-primary sample, labelled by host subfield and entry year and sorted by host-vocabulary share (x-axis, fraction). Green bars are rooted entries and grey bars are non-rooted entries. The dashed line marks the mean share of the non-rooted entries, and rooted bars are annotated with their share and number of newcomer papers. (a) Wireless backhaul (broad, CS): 14 entries, one rooted (Aerospace Engineering 2008, share 0.084, 6 newcomers) against a non-rooted mean of 0.021. (b) Einstein&ndash;Podolsky&ndash;Rosen (EPR) steering (broad, Physics): 7 entries, one rooted (Artificial Intelligence 2011, 0.142, 37 newcomers; co-transfer 0) against a non-rooted mean of 0.027. (c) Locally repairable code (localised, CS): a single co-primary entry, rooted (0.056, 3 newcomers), so there is no within-concept contrast. (d) Holographic QCD (localised, Physics): 5 entries, none rooted (mean 0.041; three have co-transfer 1.0), including an AMO Physics entry at 0.132 that did not take root. In (a) and (b), the rooted entry has a higher host-vocabulary share than every non-rooted entry of the same concept. The panels are descriptive, so no intervals are drawn.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n\n</section>\n\n<!-- ═══════════════════ LIMITATIONS ═══════════════════ -->\n<section id=\"limitations\" class=\"limitations\">\n  <h2>Limitations</h2>\n  <dl>\n    <dt>Main-arm folds used in development</dt>\n    <dd>The Screen and Held-out folds were both used during pipeline development: event counts, population sizes, and gating decisions were computed on both folds before grafting outcomes were read. Estimates on both are development-set results, not true held-out confirmations. The independent evidence for the host-vocabulary effect comes from the MeSH replication.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Population bias</dt>\n    <dd>The concept pool is dominated by physics, physical-sciences, and computer-science concepts from arXiv. The MeSH population covers only biomedicine-to-biomedicine entries. Generalisation to social sciences, humanities, or engineering is untested.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Primary specification underpowered</dt>\n    <dd>The fully saturated specification with concept-by-year and host-by-year fixed effects is inconclusive on the Held-out fold (IRR 0.98, 30 clusters). The MeSH replication and the development-set estimates rest on the co-primary specification, which leaves more residual variation.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Single-paper entries</dt>\n    <dd>87% of co-primary Screen events involve a single entry-year paper. The pooled multi-team effect is positive (IRR 1.28, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.48), but the Held-out fold alone is underpowered for this test.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Binary establishment null</dt>\n    <dd>The host-vocabulary share predicts newcomer count and probability of any uptake, but binary establishment (at least five newcomer papers in at least three of five years) is null on the Held-out fold (<em>p</em> = 0.16). The effect is graded, not threshold-based.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Cluster-robust inference</dt>\n    <dd>The cluster-robust variance estimator rejects 10&ndash;11% of null shuffles in simulation (target 5%). Wild-cluster bootstrap and permutation tests give consistent results (Held-out wild <em>p</em> = 0.012, permutation <em>p</em> = 0.026), but standard <em>p</em>-values should not be taken at face value.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Host-specificity caveat</dt>\n    <dd>The Balassa-index lift measure used to test host-specificity has a within-fixed-effect correlation of 0.997 with the log of the continuous host-vocabulary share. The lift test confirms the continuous measure rather than providing independent evidence.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Adopter evidence not independently confirmed</dt>\n    <dd>The adopter-level enrichment (OR 3.09) is Screen-fold only. The design cannot separate absorptive capacity from topical proximity.</dd>\n\n    <dt>Closure caveats</dt>\n    <dd>The Held-out fold was used in pipeline development, so the closure result is a development-set estimate. The matching falls back to Screen controls for 17 of 25 unique controls, so the estimator is not fully control-side independent. The MeSH closure result is directional under the sensitivity label but null under the primary label.</dd>\n  </dl>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ═══════════════════ CODE ARTIFACTS ═══════════════════ from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

```
        headings = await page.evaluate("""() => {

            }));
        }""")

        prev_level = 0
        for h in headings:
            level = int(h['tag'][1])

            marker = " *** SKIP ***" if skip else ""
            print(f"  {h['tag']}: {h['text']}{marker}")
            prev_level = level

        # 2. Check all images have alt text
        imgs = await page.evaluate("""() => {
            return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).map(i => ({
                src: i.src.split('/').pop(),
                alt: i.alt,
                hasAlt: i.hasAttribute('alt')
            }));
        }""")

        for img in imgs:
            status = "OK" if img['hasAlt'] and img['alt'] else "MISSING"
            print(f"  [{status}] {img['src']}: {img['alt'][:60] if img['alt'] else '(none)'}")

        # 3. Check skip link exists
        skip = await page.query_selector('.skip-link')

                main: document.querySelectorAll('main').length,
                footer: document.querySelectorAll('footer').length
            };
        }""")
        print(f"\n=== LANDMARKS === nav:{landmarks['nav']} main:{landmarks['main']} footer:{landmarks['footer']}")

        print("\n=== TAB ORDER ===")

        for i in range(20):
            focused = await page.evaluate("""() => {
                const el = document.activeElement;
                return {
                    tag: el.tagName,
                    text: (el.textContent || '').trim().substring(0, 50),
                    role: el.getAttribute('role') || '',
                    ariaLabel: el.getAttribute('aria-label') || ''
                };
            }""")

            await page.keyboard.press("Tab")

        # 6. Test lightbox: click first gallery item, check dialog opens
        print("\n=== LIGHTBOX TEST ===")
        gallery_btn = await page.query_selector('.gallery-fig .fig-trigger')
        if gallery_btn:

            await page.wait_for_timeout(200)
            lb_visible = await page.evaluate("!document.getElementById('lightbox').hidden")
            print(f"  Lightbox opened: {lb_visible}")

            # Check focus is on close button

                return document.activeElement.classList.contains('lightbox-close');

        print(f"  Lightbox role={lb_role}, aria-modal={lb_modal}, aria-label={lb_label}")

        await browser.close()
```

````
# Paper presentation page

Public web page for the paper "Host vocabulary predicts whether new scientific concepts take root across disciplinary boundaries."

## What was done

Built a single self-contained `index.html` that presents the paper's findings in a format optimised for quick comprehension. The page includes:

- **Hero** with the paper title, a plain-language TL;DR, and links to the paper PDF, code repository, research report, executive summary, and round reports.
- **Contributions** as five scannable cards, each with inline code links to the corresponding experiments and evaluations.
- **Method** walkthrough with the study design figure (Figure 1), covering data assembly, co-word network construction, the matched event study for emergence precursors, and the PPML regression for host-entry grafting.
- **Results** presenting the pre-registered findings: persistent-neighbour closure (panel coefficient −1.07, Holm p = 0.015), host-vocabulary grafting (MeSH co-primary IRR 1.23, pooled IVW IRR 1.26), mechanism decomposition (extensive margin +6.4 pp/SD, intensive IRR 1.18), and adopter enrichment (OR 3.09).
- **Figure gallery** with all six paper figures, each with its full caption and click-to-enlarge lightbox.
- **Limitations** as stated by the paper.
- **Code artifacts list** linking every experiment and dataset in the run.
- **Footer** repeating all document and round-report links.

Sticky side navigation (desktop) / horizontal top bar (mobile) with scroll-spy highlighting.

## Layout

```
index.html          Self-contained page (HTML + inline CSS + JS)
paper.tex           The final paper (source of all claims and numbers)
paper.pdf           Compiled paper
references.bib      Bibliography
figures/
  fig1_v0.jpg       Study design and analysis pipeline
  fig2_v0.jpg       Co-word network snapshot
  fig3_v0.pdf       Pre-emergence closure (vector)
  fig3_v0.png       Pre-emergence closure (rendered at 200 DPI)
  fig4_v0.pdf       Host-vocabulary effect (vector)
  fig4_v0.png       Host-vocabulary effect (rendered at 200 DPI)
  fig5_v0.pdf       Margin decomposition (vector)
  fig5_v0.png       Margin decomposition (rendered at 200 DPI)
  fig6_v0.pdf       Representative cases (vector)
  fig6_v0.png       Representative cases (rendered at 200 DPI)
workspace/          LaTeX scratch folder (not used by the page)
```

## How to run

Open `index.html` in any modern browser. No build step, no dependencies, no network required. All CSS and JavaScript are inline; the only external references are the figure images in `figures/`.

## Restoring removed files

No files were marked for deletion.
````
